claims.reason: Backed only in part: the NHS page ties its one-hour figure to winding down (line 107) and gives no hour figure for devices, only 'right before going to bed' (line 123), and the Chang abstract tests reading 'in the hours before bedtime' with no threshold. Not backed: no snapshot states that no scientifically established one-hour limit exists for all devices. The abstract-only Chang snapshot cannot show such an absence, and the NHS page does not discuss the evidence base for any time limit.

quotes.text: Chang AM, Aeschbach D, Duffy JF, Czeisler CA.
Here we compare the biological effects of reading an electronic book on a light-emitting device (LE-eBook) with reading a printed book in the hours before bedtime

claims.reason: The Chang snapshot is abstract-only. It speaks only of 'Participants' and gives no number of participants, no health status and no age. The full text of the PNAS article would be needed to check 12 healthy young adults.

claims.reason: The quote shows that the same participants were compared across the two reading conditions (a within-participant comparison, consistent with a crossover). The abstract does not use the words randomised or crossover and does not say how the order of conditions was assigned. Full text needed for the randomisation and the design label.

claims.reason: The Chang snapshot is abstract-only. It does not state the size of the exposure, the laboratory setting or anything on brief use at home, and it reports no effect size. The NHS page does not discuss exposure duration or setting. Full text of the PNAS article would be needed to check the exposure and setting, and it would still not state the caveat itself.

scope_gaps.note: The Chang abstract concerns reading an e-book on a light-emitting device in the hours before bedtime; the NHS page names television and devices 'like smartphones' right before bed. The title's 'jasne ekrany' is broader than the single device type described in the abstract.

'Warunek ekranu' is the light-emitting e-reader condition of the study; the abstract does not extend the result to phones, night mode or other screens. The sentence does not claim that, a reader might assume it.
Sample size, setting and design label are not in the abstract-only snapshot, so 'małe' and 'w kontrolowanych warunkach laboratoryjnych' are not checked.
Neither snapshot says whether a one-hour limit has or has not been established by research; the sentence presents that absence as a fact.
